body:
## Result

Skill: proposal-review. Review ID: proposal-review-r3. Review status: approved. Vision alignment: aligned. Material findings: none. Open blockers: none. Scope-preservation result: pass. Recommended proposal edits: none required. Recording mode: formal-lifecycle/manual, bounded delegated review; durable_recording_context=true; assembly PRR1G-recorded-context-gated.

## Review dimensions

- Challenge: pass. Fragmented delivery ownership and competing generation/install paths remain concrete problems. The System candidate language describes the pre-change insufficiency; its prospective amendments are not evidence of completed Distribution adoption.
- Goals: pass. A coherent supported source-to-installed path and accessible owner remain the desired outcomes. The latest user refinement deliberately removes managed-state interpretation as well as creation and automatic upgrades.
- Scope: pass. All four original goals remain in this initiative: combined model, superseded-source removal, complete current OpenCode withdrawal and bounded stale-script cleanup. Destination conflict preflight and explicit replacement are clearly in scope. Script cleanup remains limited to delivery/withdrawal, not a repository-wide deletion exercise.
- Governing principle: pass. One accountable delivery owner remains distinct from local execution permission and public publication authority.
- Direction: pass. Actual verified destination units determine conflict; shared parents are excluded. Default conflicts include empty/identical units and block the entire installation. Explicit --force replaces complete candidate units, preserves unrelated content and does not bypass integrity/path safety. Project state is neither read nor an admission marker. These deliberate choices supersede both earlier reviewed read-only/no-op behavior and the intervening unreviewed marker policy.
- Feasibility: pass. Exactly one embedded Feasibility section identifies generator, manifest, installer, source and Release boundaries. Existing filesystem/archive tooling provides a credible implementation basis without a new platform. Concrete replacement isolation and partial-failure realization belong to Design assessment; proposal approval does not certify those mechanisms. Removed state-writing/managed-upgrade machinery is not required merely because it exists in current code.
- Material impact: pass. OpenCode withdrawal, default repeated-install conflicts, explicit loss of local/obsolete contents within force-replaced units and potentially stale untouched state are disclosed. The compatibility break remains subject to Release's versioning and publication authority. This proposal does not authorize force execution in this repository.
- Vision alignment: pass; aligned. One inspectable owner and explicit authority/failure boundaries support reviewable engineering. Installer state removal does not remove Workflow/Record Format's durable engineering evidence or resumption contract.
- Downstream authority: pass. The explicit conflict policy is the user-selected product boundary, not premature sequencing or proof design. Design still owns exact replacement realization, source/consumer dispositions and recovery semantics. Delivery owns concrete implementation/proof allocation. The proposal neither approves a deletion list nor waives independent review.
- Requested decision: pass. The final decision includes all original goals plus state interpretation/writer/automatic-upgrade removal and default-conflict/explicit-force behavior, with retained-target protection and historical preservation.

## Scope preservation and specialized gates

All four initial outcomes and the successive explicit user refinements remain required; implementation slices do not defer them. scope_budget_context=true: core work, separate implementation slices and shared dependencies are clear. The nonstandard treatment explicit user refinement is accepted because it also says in scope, names the exact outcome, and has no downstream ambiguity or hidden deferral. vision_exception_context=false and standing_artifact_context=false: current VISION and Constitution exist, with no material conflict or bootstrap exception.

## Independence, basis and history

The separately delegated distribution-proposal-reviewer authored none of the proposal. Parent distribution-proposal-author authored the original and distribution-design-author authored the user-directed revisions. This reviewer changes only its assessment evidence. Prior proposal-review and proposal-review-r2 remain historical on their original subjects and stale for this direction; no prior approval is retargeted.

The complete current proposal and VISION were read, with prior full governing/source reads and fresh identity checks on linked factual basis. System/Release amendments were inspected as affected direction context, not already-approved Distribution behavior. Direct source/code inspection supplies the named implementation basis because the project map is stale in this area. Earlier source-shape findings concerned a now-withdrawn read-only compatibility design; they do not mandate reinstating an explicitly removed parser.

## Recording, limitations and handoff

Recording status: recorded when the targeted CLI save succeeds. Review path: docs/changes/2026-09-10-distribution-model-and-opencode-retirement/reviews/proposal-review-r3.json. No finding record is required. Recommendation: approve direction for its separately authorized independent Design assessment. This record itself performs no automatic downstream handoff, route mutation, implementation, adoption, final verification or publication. Concrete force replacement safety remains a Design question, not an assumed implementation success.

The current author force-boundary prose/structure checks are bounded authoring observations. The unchanged 33 legacy prose errors remain an explicitly failed baseline, not a pass or a waiver for later Verify. No runtime test or final Design claim is made by this proposal review.
independence_basis: Separate delegated nonauthor reviewer assessed the complete revised proposal and factual/governing basis; parent authored every proposal revision. No reviewed-content edits.
